_meta.description: Obesity System Explorer — full Foresight map data

nodes.label: Availability of Passive Entertainment Options
nodes.definition: Availability of recreational options that involve only limited physical exercise (tv, computer games)

nodes.label: Self-Esteem
nodes.definition: Sense of purpose and self-confidence of individuals

nodes.label: Media Availability
nodes.definition: Availability of media across formats

nodes.label: F2F Social Interaction
nodes.definition: Intensity of face-to-face interaction between individuals

nodes.label: Sociocultural Valuation of Food
nodes.definition: Degree to which food is positively valued within a given socio-cultural group

nodes.label: Media Consumption
nodes.definition: Degree to which people make use of the media offerings

nodes.label: Acculturation
nodes.definition: Degree to which a (dominant) culture is assimilated

nodes.label: TV Watching
nodes.definition: Time spent watching tv

nodes.label: Food Literacy
nodes.definition: Degree to which people are able to assess nutritional quality and provenance

nodes.label: Importance of Ideal Body-Size Image
nodes.definition: Degree to which there is a dominant image of an ideal body size in a society

nodes.label: Individualism
nodes.definition: Weakness of social fabric

nodes.label: Perceived Lack of Time
nodes.definition: By all citizens, particularly those engaged in economic activity

nodes.label: Parental Modelling of Activity
nodes.definition: Degree to which parents act as a role model in physical activity related behavioural patterns

nodes.label: Peer Pressure
nodes.definition: Degree to which average citizens influence one another’s choices

nodes.label: Conceptualisation of Obesity as a Disease
nodes.atlasVariable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease
nodes.definition: Degree to which people consider obesity to be a abnormal deviation from the healthy norm

nodes.label: Parental Control
nodes.definition: Level of control exerted by parents on children’s choices

nodes.label: Stress
nodes.definition: Perceived level of stress by individuals

nodes.label: Degree of Innate Activity in Childhood
nodes.atlasVariable: Degree of innate activity in childhood
nodes.definition: Degree to which physical activity is part of typical childhood behaviour

nodes.label: Learned Activity Patterns in Early Childhood
nodes.atlasVariable: Learned activity patterns in early childhood
nodes.definition: Degree of activity experienced by the foetus, newborn and child in early life through parental physical activity

nodes.label: Smoking Cessation
nodes.definition: Number of people quitting smoking

nodes.label: Children's Control of Diet
nodes.definition: Degree to which children exert influence on dietary choices in a family

nodes.label: Perceived Inconsistency of Science-Based Messages
nodes.definition: Degree to which there is incompatibility between scientific assessments on food related issues which (are perceived) to be similar

nodes.label: Societal Pressure to Consume
nodes.definition: Endemic pressure (via a variety of channels and actors) to consume

nodes.label: Psychological Ambivalence
nodes.definition: Degree to which people experience a psychological conflict between what people desire (e.g. fatty, sweet foods) and the need to stay healthy

nodes.label: Effort to Increase Efficiency of Consumption
nodes.atlasVariable: Effort to increase efficiency of consumption
nodes.definition: By consumers

nodes.label: Demand for Indulgence/Compensation
nodes.definition: Strenght of demand for psychological release after stress or effort

nodes.label: Degree of Physical Education
nodes.definition: Degree to which people have learned to use their body (for labour, leisure and transport)

nodes.label: Sociocultural Valuation of Activity
nodes.definition: Degree to which physical activity is positively valued in a given socio-cultural group

nodes.label: Pressure on Job Performance
nodes.definition: Pressure on employees, as generic production factors in an industrial economy

nodes.label: Pressure for Growth & Profitability
nodes.definition: Degree to which economic actors are led in their decisions by financial measures of performance

nodes.label: Food Exposure
nodes.definition: The number of food cues individuals are confronted with on a daily basis

nodes.label: Access to Opportunities for Physical Exercise
nodes.atlasVariable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise
nodes.definition: Physical accessibility (distance, safety) of opportunities for physical exercise

nodes.label: Cost of Physical Exercise
nodes.definition: Financial cost of physical recreation

nodes.label: Desire to Resolve Tension
nodes.definition: Desire to resolve psychological conflict between what people desire and what they need to stay healthy

nodes.label: Tendency to Graze
nodes.definition: Tendency to eat outside fixed meal times

nodes.label: Food Abundance
nodes.definition: The aggregate amount of food (volume) that is at any moment in time available in UK society

nodes.label: Effort to Increase Efficiency of Production
nodes.atlasVariable: Effort to increase efficiency of production
nodes.definition: Effort by economic actors (industry)

nodes.label: Conscious Control of Accumulation
nodes.definition: Level at which cognitive/reflexive processes exert influence on energy intake and expenditure

nodes.label: De-skilling
nodes.definition: The degree to which individuals are not able anymore to engage independently in routine tasks for daily living (such as cooking)

nodes.label: Pressure to Improve Access to Food Offerings
nodes.atlasVariable: Pressure to improve access to food offerings
nodes.definition: Industry-internal drive to bring food offerings as closely as possible to consumers

nodes.label: Level of Recreational Activity
nodes.definition: Degree to which people engage in physical activity for recreation

nodes.label: NEAT Non-Volitional Activity
nodes.definition: extent to which people engage in non-volitional activity (twitching etc)

nodes.label: Demand for Convenience
nodes.definition: Consumer demand for convenient (time/effort saving) food offerings

nodes.label: Desire to Minimise Cost
nodes.definition: Industry-internal drive to minimise the cost of production

nodes.label: Desire to Maximise Volume
nodes.definition: Industry-internal drive to maximise volumes sold on the market

nodes.label: Convenience of Food Offerings
nodes.definition: The degree to which food offerings cater to the desire for convenience

nodes.label: Pressure to Cater for Acquired Tastes
nodes.atlasVariable: Pressure to cater for acquired taste
nodes.definition: Industry-internal pressure to calibrate food offerings to what consumers are used to/like

nodes.label: Level of Domestic Activity
nodes.definition: Level of physical activity exhibited in the domestic arena

nodes.label: Reliance on Labour-Saving Devices & Services
nodes.definition: Reliance on labour-saving devices for daily chores

nodes.label: Social Depreciation of Labour
nodes.definition: Degree to which manual labour is negatively valued in a given socio-cultural group

nodes.label: Food Variety
nodes.definition: The number of different food products (natural and processed) available at any moment in time

nodes.label: Cost of Ingredients
nodes.definition: Cost of ingredients used in processed foodstuffs

nodes.label: Standardisation of Food Offerings
nodes.definition: Degree to which processed foodstuffs are based on similar production processes, ingredients and market positioning

nodes.label: Desire to Differentiate Food Offerings
nodes.definition: Industry-internal drive to distinguish themselves from competition

nodes.label: Tendency to Preserve Energy
nodes.definition: Tendency of people to reduce expenditure of bodily energy

nodes.label: Importance of Physical Need
nodes.definition: Degree to which physical need for energy triggers energy spending and acquiring behaviour

nodes.label: Effort to Acquire Energy
nodes.definition: Effort people spend to acquire bodily energy via food intake

nodes.label: Level of Occupational Activity
nodes.definition: Level of physical activity associated to professional duties

nodes.label: Dominance of Sedentary Employment
nodes.definition: Degree to which average citizens influence one another’s choices

nodes.label: Physical Activity
nodes.definition: Level of physical activity people engage in

nodes.label: Strength of Lock-in to Accumulate Energy
nodes.atlasVariable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy
nodes.definition: Degree to which behavioural patterns to spend and acquire energy are psychologically, biologically, institutionally locked in

nodes.label: Force of Dietary Habits
nodes.definition: The degree to which behavioural patterns related to food intake are dictated by routine and habit

nodes.label: Safety of Unmotorised Transport
nodes.definition: Level of risk for harm by engaging in non-motorised transport

nodes.label: Level of Transport Activity
nodes.definition: Level of physical activity associated to transport

nodes.label: Dominance of Motorised Transport
nodes.definition: Degree to which motorised transport dominates other ways of transport

nodes.label: Energy-Density of Food Offerings
nodes.definition: Number of calories per unit food weight

nodes.label: Level of Available Energy
nodes.definition: Level of energy available to an individual

nodes.label: Functional Fitness
nodes.definition: Level of physical fitness to perform daily tasks

nodes.label: Opportunity for Unmotorised Transport
nodes.definition: Availability of facilities/infrastructure for unmotorised transport

nodes.label: Ambient Temperature
nodes.definition: average environmental temperature indoors

nodes.label: Rate of Eating
nodes.definition: Time-span devoted to consuming a meal

nodes.label: Degree of Primary Appetite Control
nodes.atlasVariable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain
nodes.definition: Degree to which the brain automatically (non-consciously) responds to signals of the digestive system to control type and amount of food intake

nodes.label: Level of Satiety
nodes.definition: Degree to which food digestion and absorption in the gut reduces the need for food intake

nodes.label: Reliance on Surgical Interventions
nodes.definition: Reliance on pharma & surgical remedies to deal with effects of obesity

nodes.label: Degree of Optimal GI Signalling
nodes.definition: Degree of intestinal signals resulting from digestion and absorption of food that help to control the intake of type and amount of foods.

nodes.label: Resting Metabolic Rate
nodes.definition: Degree of energy utilised by the metabolism in a resting state (no physical nor intestinal activity)

nodes.label: Level of Adipocyte Metabolism
nodes.definition: Degree to which fat is rapidly absorbed and stored in adipose tissue (fat storage cells)

nodes.label: Level of Thermogenesis
nodes.definition: Degree of energy needed to maintain body temperature

nodes.label: Extent of Digestion and Absorption
nodes.definition: Degree of optimal energy and nutrient absorption by the human body

nodes.label: Level of Infections
nodes.definition: Degree of general occurrence of all type of diseases in society

nodes.label: Level of Fat-Free Mass
nodes.definition: Relative level of fat-free tissue (muscle) in comparison to fat tissue (adipose tissue)

nodes.label: Genetic and/or Epigenetic Predisposition to Obesity
nodes.atlasVariable: Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity
nodes.definition: Degree to which a person is predisposed by his genetic make-up to develop obesity; degree of indirect inheritance that contributes to obesity susceptibility

nodes.label: Appropriateness of Nutrient Partitioning
nodes.definition: Degree to which the body is able to maintain the appropriate balance between fat, protein and carbohydrate metabolism and storage

nodes.label: Appropriateness of Maternal Body Composition
nodes.definition: Degree to which the maternal body has the optimal physiological condition at conception, pregnancy and birth

nodes.label: Quality & Quantity of Breast Feeding (and Weaning)
Appropriateness of Child Growth
nodes.definition: Degree to which speed of growth and physiological status of the child are in balance with each other and thus to prevent early onset of adipose tissue formation

nodes.label: Appropriateness of Embryonic & Fetal Growth
nodes.definition: Degree to which the physiological environment for the embryo provides optimal nutrient and physical environment for growth

child.text: Looking back at the first 12 months, which feeding pattern best fits the persona?

options.label: A
options.text: Breastfeeding was sustained, with gradual varied weaning and responsive feeding.

options.label: B
options.text: Mixed feeding with broadly timely weaning and some convenience foods.

options.label: C
options.text: Brief or inconsistent breastfeeding, followed by a narrow range of familiar foods.

options.label: D
options.text: Highly disrupted feeding, very early solids, sweetened feeds or prolonged bottle dependence.

child.text: Across early childhood health checks, how has the persona's growth generally tracked?

options.label: A
options.text: Steady, proportionate growth with consistent height, weight and development.

options.label: B
options.text: Small fluctuations but broadly proportionate growth.

options.label: C
options.text: Weight rose faster than height for sustained periods or repeated catch-up growth occurred.

options.label: D
options.text: Markedly rapid or uneven growth with repeated nutritional or medical concern.

child.text: What is known about weight-related patterns in the persona's close biological family?

options.label: A
options.text: Little family history of persistent obesity, diabetes or very low activity.

effects.variable: Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity
Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: B
options.text: Some family risk, but patterns are mixed.

effects.variable: Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity
Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: C
options.text: Several close relatives have persistent obesity, diabetes or low activity.

effects.variable: Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity
Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: D
options.text: Strong multigenerational severe obesity or early metabolic disease.

effects.variable: Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity
Degree of primary appetite control by brain

child.text: When no adult is directing them, how naturally active is the persona during a typical free hour?

options.label: A
options.text: Almost constantly moving, climbing, fidgeting or inventing active play.

effects.variable: Degree of innate activity in childhood

options.label: B
options.text: Alternates naturally between active and quiet play.

effects.variable: Degree of innate activity in childhood

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly chooses seated play and needs prompting to move.

effects.variable: Degree of innate activity in childhood

options.label: D
options.text: Strongly avoids movement unless an adult structures it.

effects.variable: Degree of innate activity in childhood

child.text: On a typical weekend, what activity pattern do the adults at home model?

options.label: A
options.text: Adults routinely walk, exercise or play actively with the child.

effects.variable: Learned activity patterns in early childhood

options.label: B
options.text: Adults are moderately active and sometimes include the child.

effects.variable: Learned activity patterns in early childhood

options.label: C
options.text: Adults mostly rest or use screens while telling the child to be active.

effects.variable: Learned activity patterns in early childhood

options.label: D
options.text: Adults strongly avoid physical effort and choose the least active option.

effects.variable: Learned activity patterns in early childhood

child.text: At weekday meals, how do caregivers guide what and how much the persona eats?

options.label: A
options.text: Balanced structure, choices within boundaries, and hunger/fullness guide stopping.

options.label: B
options.text: Generally structured meals with occasional bargaining or finish-your-plate pressure.

options.label: C
options.text: Rules vary; adults often negotiate bites, use treats or override fullness.

options.label: D
options.text: Meals are highly controlling or almost entirely unbounded.

child.text: When choosing snacks, drinks or a family meal, how much influence does the persona usually have?

options.label: A
options.text: Can express preferences, but adults hold clear boundaries.

options.label: B
options.text: Usually chooses from an adult-curated shortlist.

options.label: C
options.text: Pester power frequently changes purchases, especially branded snacks or bubble tea.

options.label: D
options.text: The child largely determines purchases and meal venues.

child.text: On most school nights, how are the persona's meals prepared?

options.label: A
options.text: Cooked from basic ingredients with deliberate vegetables, protein and less sauce.

options.label: B
options.text: Mix of home cooking and simple convenience items.

options.label: C
options.text: Usually dabao, delivered, reheated or assembled with little ingredient knowledge.

options.label: D
options.text: Almost entirely ready-to-eat food; few adults can cook a basic balanced meal.

child.text: Before school on a typical weekday, what does breakfast look like?

options.label: A
options.text: Regular filling breakfast with protein or fruit and little added sugar.

options.label: B
options.text: Regular but simple breakfast with limited variety.

options.label: C
options.text: Often rushed, sweet or eaten on the move; skipped once or twice weekly.

options.label: D
options.text: Usually skipped or replaced by a sweet drink or impulse purchase.

child.text: At the school canteen on a typical day, what does the selected meal most often resemble?

options.label: A
options.text: Balanced meal with vegetables, sensible staple, protein and water.

options.label: B
options.text: Reasonable main meal, but vegetables or wholegrains are inconsistent.

options.label: C
options.text: Refined-starch-heavy or fried meal with little fibre and a sweet drink.

options.label: D
options.text: Mostly fried snacks or sweet drinks rather than a complete meal.

child.text: When served a larger-than-usual portion, what usually happens?

options.label: A
options.text: Notices fullness, leaves food when satisfied, and adults accept it.

effects.variable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: B
options.text: Usually eats most but may stop with some food left.

effects.variable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: C
options.text: Finishes because it is served, expected or wasting food feels wrong.

effects.variable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: D
options.text: Reliably finishes and often asks for more before fullness registers.

effects.variable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain

child.text: During a typical weekday dinner, how does the persona eat?

options.label: A
options.text: Seated with others, without a screen, at a conversational pace.

options.label: B
options.text: Usually with family, though a television may be on or eating is hurried.

options.label: C
options.text: Often quickly while watching a device or doing homework.

options.label: D
options.text: Regularly rushes alone in front of a screen with little awareness of pace.

child.text: Between school ending and bedtime, how often does the persona eat outside planned meals?

options.label: A
options.text: Rarely; usually one planned snack and food is not continuously visible.

options.label: B
options.text: One or two snacks at set times, with occasional extra bites.

options.label: C
options.text: Grazes through homework, tuition or screen time when snacks are within reach.

options.label: D
options.text: Near-continuous eating via cupboards, vending, convenience stores or delivery.

child.text: In a typical school week, how often does the persona choose sweetened drinks such as bubble tea or canned drinks?

options.label: A
options.text: Less than once weekly; water is the default.

options.label: B
options.text: Once or twice weekly, usually smaller or less-sugar.

options.label: C
options.text: Three to five times weekly as part of the after-school routine.

options.label: D
options.text: Daily or more; sweet drinks are the normal hydration or reward.

child.text: Across a normal month, how willing is the persona to eat unfamiliar foods?

options.label: A
options.text: Willing to taste and gradually accepts a broad range.

options.label: B
options.text: Moderate range; needs repeated exposure.

options.label: C
options.text: Narrow preferred list and often rejects vegetables or mixed dishes.

options.label: D
options.text: Extremely restricted choices; a separate preferred meal is routinely provided.

child.text: On most evenings, what is the social pattern around dinner?

options.label: A
options.text: Household usually eats together without pressure, shame or reward bargaining.

options.label: B
options.text: Some family members eat together, but timing is uneven.

options.label: C
options.text: Persona often eats separately because of work, tuition or preferences.

options.label: D
options.text: Meals are largely solitary or conflictual, with screens and bargaining.

child.text: How does the persona travel to and from school on most days?

options.label: A
options.text: Walks, cycles or scooters for most of a safe journey.

options.label: B
options.text: Uses MRT or bus with a meaningful walk at both ends.

options.label: C
options.text: Driven or school bus, with only short walks.

options.label: D
options.text: Driven door-to-door and rarely walks during the journey.

child.text: During a typical school recess, what does the persona usually do after eating?

options.label: A
options.text: Runs, plays games or moves with peers.

options.label: B
options.text: Mixes active play with standing and chatting.

options.label: C
options.text: Usually sits or remains near the canteen/classroom.

options.label: D
options.text: Avoids active areas and spends nearly all recess seated.

child.text: How does the persona experience PE lessons in a typical school term?

options.label: A
options.text: Participates fully, learns varied skills and feels competent.

options.label: B
options.text: Participates most of the time; engagement depends on activity.

options.label: C
options.text: Often participates minimally or feels repeatedly unsuccessful.

options.label: D
options.text: Frequently misses, avoids or is excluded and associates PE with embarrassment.

child.text: What does the persona's main CCA or structured after-school activity involve?

options.label: A
options.text: Regular moderate or vigorous movement with teamwork and skill progression.

options.label: B
options.text: Some movement, but intensity varies.

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly seated activity with only occasional active sessions.

options.label: D
options.text: No regular CCA or repeated withdrawal from movement/group activities.

child.text: On a typical weekday, how much after-school time is fixed by tuition, homework, caregiving or travel?

options.label: A
options.text: At least an hour of flexible time, with movement protected.

options.label: B
options.text: Most time scheduled, but active breaks or one free block remain.

options.label: C
options.text: Schedule is tight and outdoor play is often dropped.

options.label: D
options.text: Nearly the whole afternoon/evening is spoken for and sedentary.

child.text: On a typical school night, how much leisure screen time does the persona have?

options.label: A
options.text: Under one hour, with active and social alternatives readily available.

options.label: B
options.text: About one to two hours after homework.

options.label: C
options.text: Two to four hours, often while snacking.

options.label: D
options.text: More than four hours, displacing movement and family interaction.

child.text: During the content the persona watches most, how often are foods or drinks promoted?

options.label: A
options.text: Rarely, and caregivers discuss persuasive intent.

options.label: B
options.text: Occasionally through ordinary advertising or creators.

options.label: C
options.text: Frequently through influencers, games or promotions that shape requests.

options.label: D
options.text: Constantly; food-focused content regularly triggers requests.

child.text: When the persona wants to play outdoors near home, what is the practical situation?

options.label: A
options.text: Playgrounds, courts or park connectors are close, appealing and easy to reach.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: B
options.text: Facilities exist nearby, though timing or supervision sometimes limits use.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: C
options.text: Suitable spaces are limited, crowded or inconvenient.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: D
options.text: Adults perceive the area as unsafe or inaccessible; outdoor movement is rare.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

child.text: How affordable and logistically accessible are organised physical activities?

options.label: A
options.text: Free or low-cost school, ActiveSG or community options fit location and schedule.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: B
options.text: Options are manageable, though registration, travel or fees limit frequency.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: C
options.text: Cost, transport or caregiver timing makes participation sporadic.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: D
options.text: Activities are effectively out of reach because of fees, distance or access.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

child.text: The peers the persona spends the most free time with—what do they usually encourage?

options.label: A
options.text: Active play, sport or walking without teasing less-skilled children.

options.label: B
options.text: Mix of active and seated activities with no strong norm.

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly gaming, eating or sitting; active suggestions lose out.

options.label: D
options.text: Strong pressure to avoid sport, copy food trends or mock bodies.

child.text: When the persona is upset after school, what most often helps them settle?

options.label: A
options.text: Talking, rest, play or another non-food routine.

options.label: B
options.text: Mix of conversation, screens and an occasional comfort food.

options.label: C
options.text: Food or sweet drinks are commonly used to change the mood.

options.label: D
options.text: Eating is the dominant calming strategy alongside prolonged screens.

child.text: How is body size discussed by the adults and peers most influential to the persona?

options.label: A
options.text: Focus on health, strength and function; bodies are not ranked or mocked.

options.label: B
options.text: Occasional appearance comments, but adults correct teasing.

options.label: C
options.text: Frequent weight and shape comparison creates worry.

options.label: D
options.text: Teasing, shame or intense thinness/muscularity pressure is normalised.

child.text: When the persona asks why some foods are healthier, how do adults or school staff respond?

options.label: A
options.text: Consistent age-appropriate explanations about patterns, portions and context.

options.label: B
options.text: Broadly sound guidance, though explanations are brief.

options.label: C
options.text: Home, school, social media and healthcare messages conflict.

options.label: D
options.text: Adults rely on myths, stigma or contradictory bans.

child.text: Over the past year, how have illness and regular medicines affected activity or appetite?

options.label: A
options.text: Little illness and no meaningful medicine effects.

options.label: B
options.text: Occasional illness or short courses with temporary effects.

options.label: C
options.text: Repeated infections or regular medicine sometimes reduce activity or increase appetite.

options.label: D
options.text: Frequent illness or multiple medicines have sustained effects on appetite, energy or participation.

workingAdult.text: What is the persona's highest completed education, and how confidently do they use written health information?

options.label: A
options.text: Post-secondary/tertiary education and confident critical use of labels and guidance.

options.label: B
options.text: Secondary/vocational education with reasonable practical understanding.

options.label: C
options.text: Limited formal education or low confidence; relies on familiar rules or others.

options.label: D
options.text: Health information is difficult to access, interpret or use.

workingAdult.text: On a typical workday, how much of the job is spent seated?

options.label: A
options.text: Less than one-quarter; sustained walking, lifting, standing or hands-on work.

options.label: B
options.text: One-quarter to one-half, with movement built into tasks.

options.label: C
options.text: One-half to three-quarters, with long seated blocks.

options.label: D
options.text: More than three-quarters, often uninterrupted meetings, driving or computer work.

workingAdult.text: During the busiest part of a typical week, how manageable does the workload feel?

options.label: A
options.text: Predictable enough to protect meals, movement breaks and finishing time.

options.label: B
options.text: Busy periods occur, but control and recovery are usually retained.

options.label: C
options.text: Deadlines regularly crowd out breaks, meal planning or exercise.

options.label: D
options.text: Work feels persistently urgent and uncontrollable with little recovery.

workingAdult.text: On a typical workday evening, how much time is committed to overtime, caregiving, chores or travel?

options.label: A
options.text: At least two flexible hours remain for food, movement and rest.

options.label: B
options.text: About one flexible hour usually remains.

options.label: C
options.text: Very little flexible time; convenient meals and sedentary recovery are common.

options.label: D
options.text: Evening is almost entirely spoken for and time scarcity is continuous.

workingAdult.text: How does the persona travel for the main work commute on most days?

options.label: A
options.text: Walks or cycles for most of a practical, safe journey.

options.label: B
options.text: Uses MRT/bus with 20–30 minutes of walking round trip.

options.label: C
options.text: Uses public transport but minimises walking through feeders or ride-hailing.

options.label: D
options.text: Travels mainly by car, taxi, motorcycle or door-to-door transport.

workingAdult.text: During long periods of sitting at work, what does the persona usually do?

options.label: A
options.text: Gets up every 30–60 minutes and walks for routine tasks.

options.label: B
options.text: Takes a few planned breaks and accumulates some incidental walking.

options.label: C
options.text: Remains seated for two to three hours unless forced to move.

options.label: D
options.text: Rarely breaks sitting and uses services/devices to avoid small movements.

workingAdult.text: Around the workplace and route home, what food environment does the persona encounter?

options.label: A
options.text: Balanced meals are easy to find and snacks/promotions are not constantly visible.

options.label: B
options.text: Broad mix of hawker, food-court and convenience options requiring deliberate choice.

options.label: C
options.text: Cheap visible snacks, sweet drinks and energy-dense meals are easiest.

options.label: D
options.text: Food is continuously available through vending, delivery and promotions.

workingAdult.text: Near home, how easy is it to be active after work?

options.label: A
options.text: Safe routes, park connectors, ActiveSG facilities or affordable classes are close.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: B
options.text: Several options exist, though weather or opening times sometimes interfere.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: C
options.text: Facilities require travel, feel costly or walking routes are fragmented.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: D
options.text: Few safe, affordable or accessible opportunities are perceived.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

workingAdult.text: In the household, who usually handles cooking, cleaning, laundry and errands?

options.label: A
options.text: Persona shares or performs substantial hands-on household work.

options.label: B
options.text: Tasks are shared with moderate use of appliances, delivery or help.

options.label: C
options.text: Most tasks are outsourced or automated; little routine domestic movement.

options.label: D
options.text: Nearly all food, cleaning and errands are handled by services or others.

workingAdult.text: On a typical workday, where do the main meals come from?

options.label: A
options.text: Mostly home-prepared or deliberately assembled, with ingredients and portions visible.

options.label: B
options.text: Mix of home food and familiar hawker/food-court meals.

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly dabao, delivery or convenience meals chosen for speed.

options.label: D
options.text: Almost entirely ready-to-eat, delivered or fast-food meals.

workingAdult.text: What does the typical weekday lunch or dinner plate look like?

options.label: A
options.text: Substantial vegetables, moderate staple, protein and little fried/heavy sauce.

options.label: B
options.text: Broadly balanced, but vegetables or wholegrains are inconsistent.

options.label: C
options.text: Refined starch and richer protein dominate with limited vegetables.

options.label: D
options.text: Mostly fried, processed or energy-dense food with very little fibre.

workingAdult.text: When ordering cai fan, noodles or a set meal, how does the persona handle portion size?

options.label: A
options.text: Chooses modest staple, avoids upsizing and can leave food when full.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: B
options.text: Usually accepts the standard portion.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: C
options.text: Often adds rice, noodles, sides or a larger drink.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: D
options.text: Regularly chooses large/double portions and finishes regardless of fullness.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

workingAdult.text: How does the persona eat lunch on a typical busy workday?

options.label: A
options.text: Takes a real break away from work and eats slowly enough to notice fullness.

options.label: B
options.text: Usually pauses work but finishes within 15–20 minutes.

options.label: C
options.text: Often eats quickly at the desk, in a vehicle or between meetings.

options.label: D
options.text: Regularly rushes, multitasks or delays until extremely hungry.

workingAdult.text: Between breakfast and bedtime, how often does the persona snack outside planned eating times?

options.label: A
options.text: Rarely, or once because of genuine hunger.

options.label: B
options.text: One or two portioned snacks.

options.label: C
options.text: Frequent small bites during work, commuting or screens.

options.label: D
options.text: Near-continuous grazing through pantry, vending, delivery or convenience stores.

workingAdult.text: How fixed is the persona's weekday eating routine?

options.label: A
options.text: Regular but flexible; choices and portions adapt to circumstances.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: B
options.text: Familiar routine with occasional healthier substitutions.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: C
options.text: Repeats the same stalls, drinks and snack times even without hunger.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: D
options.text: Routine feels locked in and changing usual rewards creates strong resistance.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

workingAdult.text: Across a normal week, how varied are the persona's meals?

options.label: A
options.text: Wide range of vegetables, proteins, staples and cuisines supporting quality.

options.label: B
options.text: Moderate variety, but several meals repeat.

options.label: C
options.text: Narrow set of preferred convenient or reliably tasty meals.

options.label: D
options.text: Highly repetitive choices driven by palatability, habit or avoidance.

workingAdult.text: In a typical week, how much alcohol does the persona drink?

options.label: A
options.text: None or less than one standard drink.

options.label: B
options.text: One to three standard drinks.

options.label: C
options.text: Four to seven drinks or one heavier social session.

options.label: D
options.text: More than seven, frequent drinking or repeated binge episodes.

workingAdult.text: Which best describes the current smoking or vaping trajectory?

options.label: A
options.text: Never smoked, or stopped long ago with stable non-food coping.

options.label: B
options.text: Recently stopped with structured support and planned substitutes.

options.label: C
options.text: Recently stopped and frequently replaces smoking with snacks or sweet drinks.

options.label: D
options.text: Still smokes/vapes with repeated quit attempts and compensatory eating.

workingAdult.text: In a typical week, how much purposeful exercise does the persona complete?

options.label: A
options.text: At least 150 minutes moderate activity or equivalent, plus strength work.

options.label: B
options.text: About 75–149 minutes or several shorter sessions.

options.label: C
options.text: Less than 75 minutes, mostly sporadic walks or occasional classes.

options.label: D
options.text: No purposeful exercise beyond essential movement.

workingAdult.text: What is the main form of exercise or active leisure?

options.label: A
options.text: Regular social or team activity combining movement, accountability and enjoyment.

options.label: B
options.text: Mostly individual exercise with a stable routine.

options.label: C
options.text: Occasional informal activity without consistency.

options.label: D
options.text: No preferred activity; exercise feels isolating, embarrassing or unrewarding.

workingAdult.text: When the persona intends to exercise but does not, what usually blocks the plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Plans are rarely blocked; nearby backup options exist.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: B
options.text: Weather, fatigue or schedule occasionally interfere, but sessions are replaced.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: C
options.text: Time, cost, travel or safety concerns regularly cause cancellation.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: D
options.text: Multiple barriers combine and exercise is consistently judged impractical.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

workingAdult.text: How does the persona think about ordinary effort such as walking, stairs, carrying or cleaning?

options.label: A
options.text: Useful movement that counts and is often chosen deliberately.

options.label: B
options.text: Generally positive, though convenience sometimes wins.

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly an inconvenience to minimise when lifts, delivery or transport exist.

options.label: D
options.text: A sign of poor planning or low status; manual effort is strongly avoided.

workingAdult.text: Across a typical workweek, how often does the persona feel persistently tense or unable to switch off?

options.label: A
options.text: Rarely; pressure is contained and recovery routines are reliable.

options.label: B
options.text: Some days, but recovery usually occurs by the next day or weekend.

options.label: C
options.text: Most days, affecting appetite, patience or movement.

options.label: D
options.text: Almost continuously, with little control or recovery.

workingAdult.text: After a difficult day, what does the persona most often reach for?

options.label: A
options.text: Conversation, movement, rest or another non-food routine.

options.label: B
options.text: Mix of non-food coping and a modest treat.

options.label: C
options.text: Comfort food, bubble tea, alcohol or delivery is frequent compensation.

options.label: D
options.text: Large portions, grazing or alcohol are the main way to numb tension.

workingAdult.text: How does the persona generally feel about their body and weight?

options.label: A
options.text: Mostly accepting and functional; actions are not driven by shame.

options.label: B
options.text: Some dissatisfaction, but it does not dominate self-worth.

options.label: C
options.text: Frequent comparison creates cycles of strict control and disengagement.

options.label: D
options.text: Strong shame shapes social life, eating and public activity.

workingAdult.text: The people the persona spends the most free time with—what do they usually do together?

options.label: A
options.text: Mix of conversation and active plans such as walking, sport or outings.

options.label: B
options.text: Mostly social meals or coffee, with occasional active plans.

options.label: C
options.text: Predominantly seated entertainment, gaming, drinking or long meals.

options.label: D
options.text: Very little face-to-face contact; leisure is solitary and screen-based.

workingAdult.text: When the persona eats with the people they see most, what usually happens?

options.label: A
options.text: Group is comfortable ordering modestly and stopping without pressure.

options.label: B
options.text: Meals are sometimes indulgent but moderate in frequency and portion.

options.label: C
options.text: Regular pressure to order more, add drinks or match others' portions.

options.label: D
options.text: Heavy eating/drinking is central to belonging and declining attracts comment.

workingAdult.text: On a typical evening, how much leisure screen time does the persona have?

options.label: A
options.text: Under one hour, with substantial offline or active time.

options.label: B
options.text: About one to two hours after responsibilities.

options.label: C
options.text: Two to four hours, often paired with snacking.

options.label: D
options.text: More than four hours, with passive media dominating.

workingAdult.text: How often does the usual media feed prompt an immediate food or drink purchase?

options.label: A
options.text: Rarely; targeted marketing is recognised and ignored.

options.label: B
options.text: Occasionally for a planned treat or new product.

options.label: C
options.text: Often through delivery promotions, influencers or limited-time deals.

options.label: D
options.text: Very often; browsing routinely triggers unplanned orders.

workingAdult.text: When nutrition or weight advice conflicts, how does the persona respond?

options.label: A
options.text: Checks credible sources and returns to long-term principles.

options.label: B
options.text: Seeks clarification and usually settles on a reasonable approach.

options.label: C
options.text: Switches between rules and becomes unsure what to trust.

options.label: D
options.text: Feels science constantly reverses and disengages or follows persuasive claims.

workingAdult.text: When a weight-related health concern appears, what is the usual first response?

options.label: A
options.text: Seeks assessment and combines medical advice with sustainable routine changes.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: B
options.text: Consults a professional but expects medication to do much of the work.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: C
options.text: Cycles through supplements, online remedies or short programmes.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: D
options.text: Looks mainly for a medicine or procedure that bypasses contextual change.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

workingAdult.text: How do regular medicines affect appetite, energy or movement?

options.label: A
options.text: No meaningful medicine effects, or side effects are well managed.

options.label: B
options.text: One medicine may have mild effects that are monitored.

options.label: C
options.text: Medicines noticeably increase appetite, fatigue or weight with limited adjustment.

options.label: D
options.text: Multiple medicines substantially affect hunger, metabolism or function.

workingAdult.text: Which profile best captures childhood activity, eating habits and family predisposition?

options.label: A
options.text: Active childhood, varied meals and little strong family history.

Degree of innate activity in childhood
Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity

options.label: B
options.text: Mixed childhood patterns with some family risk.

effects.variable: Learned activity patterns in early childhood
Degree of innate activity in childhood
Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly sedentary childhood, entrenched energy-dense habits or several affected relatives.

effects.variable: Learned activity patterns in early childhood
Degree of innate activity in childhood
Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity

options.label: D

senior.text: On a typical weekday, what is the current work or retirement pattern?

options.label: A
options.text: Routine includes regular errands, movement and purposeful activity.

options.label: B
options.text: Mix of seated and active periods.

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly sedentary days with little movement outside essentials.

options.label: D
options.text: Highly inactive days with most time seated and few commitments.

senior.text: How predictable and manageable is the daily routine?

options.label: A
options.text: Regular meals, movement, social contact and appointments provide structure.

options.label: B
options.text: Loose routine with occasional disruption.

options.label: C
options.text: Irregular days; meals, medicines and activity shift with circumstances.

options.label: D
options.text: Little structure; long periods pass without planned meals, movement or contact.

senior.text: When walking on level ground for 10–15 minutes, what can the persona typically do?

options.label: A
options.text: Walks independently at a steady pace without rest.

options.label: B
options.text: Walks independently but slowly or needs one brief pause.

options.label: C
options.text: Needs a walking aid, accompaniment or several pauses.

options.label: D
options.text: Rarely manages this distance because of pain, breathlessness, balance or fatigue.

senior.text: When moving around the neighbourhood alone, how safe and confident does the persona feel?

options.label: A
options.text: Confident using pavements, crossings, lifts and park connectors.

options.label: B
options.text: Generally confident but avoids a few routes or busy crossings.

options.label: C
options.text: Frequently worries about falls, traffic or being stranded.

options.label: D
options.text: Feels unsafe without assistance and avoids most independent trips.

senior.text: How accessible are exercise options that suit mobility and finances?

options.label: A
options.text: Appropriate low-cost Active Ageing Centre, ActiveSG or walking options are nearby.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: B
options.text: Options exist but timing, transport or fees limit regular attendance.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: C
options.text: Few options feel age-appropriate, affordable or accessible.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

options.label: D
options.text: No realistic opportunity because of cost, distance, access or confidence.

effects.variable: Accessibility to opportunities for physical exercise

senior.text: In a typical week, how often does the persona join a group activity involving movement?

options.label: A
options.text: Three or more times with regular social connection.

options.label: B
options.text: Once or twice, including an informal walking group.

options.label: C
options.text: Less than weekly and inconsistent.

options.label: D
options.text: Never because of opportunity, confidence, mobility or companionship.

senior.text: How much hands-on household activity occurs on a typical day?

options.label: A
options.text: Regular cooking, cleaning, laundry, gardening or errands.

options.label: B
options.text: Some daily tasks, with help for heavier chores.

options.label: C
options.text: Most chores done by family, helper or services.

options.label: D
options.text: Almost entirely dependent on others or devices for household tasks.

senior.text: For nearby errands such as the market, clinic or kopitiam, how does the persona travel?

options.label: A
options.text: Walks for most trips and uses public transport for longer distances.

options.label: B
options.text: Uses bus/MRT with some walking.

options.label: C
options.text: Usually relies on family car, taxi or ride-hailing.

options.label: D
options.text: Rarely goes out independently and is transported door-to-door.

senior.text: How does the persona usually obtain groceries and prepared food?

options.label: A
options.text: Walks or takes public transport and chooses items personally.

options.label: B
options.text: Combines in-person shopping with occasional family help or delivery.

options.label: C
options.text: Relies mainly on family, delivery apps or a helper, with limited control.

options.label: D
options.text: Food arrives almost entirely through others or institutional provision.

senior.text: How confident is the persona preparing a simple balanced meal?

options.label: A
options.text: Can plan and cook several balanced meals and adapt texture or portions.

options.label: B
options.text: Can prepare a limited set but sometimes depends on convenience items.

options.label: C
options.text: Cooking skills declined or never developed; ready meals and dabao are common.

options.label: D
options.text: Cannot or does not prepare food and has little practical nutrition knowledge.

senior.text: Where does the main meal come from on most days?

options.label: A
options.text: Home-cooked or carefully selected community meal with vegetables and protein.

options.label: B
options.text: Mix of home food and familiar hawker/kopitiam meals.

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly takeaway or convenience meals chosen for softness, price or ease.

options.label: D
options.text: Mostly processed, delivered or highly repetitive food.

senior.text: What does the typical lunch or dinner contain?

options.label: A
options.text: Adequate protein, vegetables/fruit and moderate staple.

options.label: B
options.text: Reasonable balance, though protein or vegetables are sometimes insufficient.

options.label: C
options.text: Mostly refined starch, gravy or soft processed food with limited fibre/protein.

options.label: D
options.text: Very small, nutritionally poor or energy-dense meals with little variety.

senior.text: At regular meal times, how does the persona experience hunger and fullness?

options.label: A
options.text: Hunger is predictable and fullness clear enough to stop comfortably.

effects.variable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: B
options.text: Appetite varies but suitable amounts are usually judged.

effects.variable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: C
options.text: Hunger/fullness cues are weak, delayed or confusing.

effects.variable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain

options.label: D
options.text: Appetite regulation is markedly disrupted by illness, medicine or long patterns.

effects.variable: Degree of primary appetite control by brain

senior.text: When served a standard hawker or family portion, how much is usually eaten?

options.label: A
options.text: Adjusts to appetite and is comfortable leaving or saving food.

options.label: B
options.text: Usually eats the standard portion with occasional leftovers.

options.label: C
options.text: Finishes the full portion even when appetite is low.

options.label: D
options.text: Regularly eats oversized portions or alternates between very large and skipped meals.

senior.text: How does the persona eat a typical main meal?

options.label: A
options.text: Unhurried, seated comfortably, with enough chewing and attention.

options.label: B
options.text: Moderate pace, though conversation or television distracts.

options.label: C
options.text: Often rushes or eats distracted despite dental/swallowing difficulty.

options.label: D
options.text: Very rapid or prolonged eating, with physical difficulty substantially affecting intake.

senior.text: Between meals on a typical day, what is the pattern?

options.label: A
options.text: Little unplanned eating; any snack is deliberate and useful.

options.label: B
options.text: One or two routine portioned snacks.

options.label: C
options.text: Frequent biscuits, sweets or drinks while watching television.

options.label: D
options.text: Continuous grazing because meals are skipped, appetite is uncertain or food is always near.

senior.text: How flexible is the persona when a long-standing food routine no longer suits health or appetite?

options.label: A
options.text: Adapts recipes, portions and timing while preserving familiar meaning.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: B
options.text: Makes gradual changes with family or clinician support.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: C
options.text: Finds changes difficult and returns to the same stalls, dishes and portions.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

options.label: D
options.text: Strongly resists change even when chewing, disease or medicine make it unsuitable.

effects.variable: Strength of lock-in to accumulate energy

senior.text: When the persona meets family or friends, what role does food play?

options.label: A
options.text: Supports connection but portions and frequency remain comfortable.

options.label: B
options.text: Meals are central but balanced with conversation or light activity.

options.label: C
options.text: Hospitality regularly means repeated servings, rich dishes and pressure.

options.label: D
options.text: Social contact occurs almost only through large meals/treats; refusing is disrespectful.

senior.text: In a typical week, how much alcohol does the persona drink?

options.label: A
options.text: None or less than one standard drink.

options.label: B
options.text: One to three drinks without binge episodes.

options.label: C
options.text: Four to seven drinks or occasional heavy sessions.

options.label: D
options.text: More than seven or alcohol used routinely for sleep/coping.

senior.text: Which best describes the smoking history now?

options.label: A
options.text: Never smoked, or quit long ago without compensatory eating.

options.label: B
options.text: Quit recently with structured support and manageable appetite changes.

options.label: C
options.text: Quit recently and substitutes snacks or sweet drinks.

options.label: D
options.text: Still smokes or cycles through quitting with substantial compensatory eating.

senior.text: Across a typical week, how much face-to-face contact occurs outside essential appointments?

options.label: A
options.text: Meaningful contact most days through family, neighbours or community.

options.label: B
options.text: Several contacts weekly, though some days are solitary.

options.label: C
options.text: One or two brief contacts weekly with long periods alone.

options.label: D
options.text: Almost no face-to-face contact or sense of inclusion.

senior.text: On a typical day, how much leisure time is spent watching television or using passive screens?

options.label: A
options.text: Under two hours, with regular movement and social/practical activity.

options.label: B
options.text: Two to four hours, broken up by errands or chores.

options.label: C
options.text: Four to seven hours with long uninterrupted sitting.

options.label: D
options.text: More than seven hours, filling most waking leisure time.

senior.text: When the persona feels lonely, worried or low, what most often happens next?

options.label: A
options.text: Contacts someone, goes out, moves, rests or uses another non-food strategy.

options.label: B
options.text: Mix of social contact, television and an occasional treat.

options.label: C
options.text: Often snacks, orders comfort food or remains inactive.

options.label: D
options.text: Food, alcohol or complete withdrawal is the main response for days.

senior.text: How does the persona interpret body weight in later life?

options.label: A
options.text: One health factor among many; strength, mobility and function matter most.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: B
options.text: Recognises health implications but holds some appearance assumptions.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: C
options.text: Views weight through stigma, inevitability or rigid ideals.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: D
options.text: Dismisses weight entirely as ageing or sees it as personal failure needing extremes.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

senior.text: When diet advice changes because of chronic conditions, how well can messages be reconciled?

options.label: A
options.text: Understands the purpose, asks questions and follows an integrated practical plan.

options.label: B
options.text: Understands main priorities but needs occasional clarification.

options.label: C
options.text: Different instructions feel contradictory and adherence changes weekly.

options.label: D
options.text: Feels overwhelmed or distrustful and disengages.

senior.text: When a weight-related health issue worsens, what response is preferred?

options.label: A
options.text: Clinician review integrating medicine, nutrition, mobility, function and social context.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: B
options.text: Medical treatment first, with some willingness to change routines.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: C
options.text: Repeated supplements or medicines with limited attention to context.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

options.label: D
options.text: Strong preference for a pharmaceutical/procedural fix with minimal contextual change.

effects.variable: Conceptualisation of obesity as a disease

senior.text: How complex is the regular medication regimen, and how much does it affect function?

options.label: A
options.text: Few/no medicines with meaningful appetite, energy or movement effects.

options.label: B
options.text: Several medicines, but side effects are monitored and manageable.

options.label: C
options.text: Multiple medicines cause fatigue, appetite change, dizziness or reduced activity.

options.label: D
options.text: Polypharmacy substantially shapes appetite, balance, metabolism and independence.

senior.text: Over the past year, how have infections, hospital stays or prolonged illness affected the persona?

options.label: A
options.text: Little disruption; strength and activity return quickly.

options.label: B
options.text: One short episode with temporary reduction.

options.label: C
options.text: Repeated illness/admission led to noticeable deconditioning or muscle loss.

options.label: D
options.text: Frequent/severe illness caused persistent frailty and loss of independence.

options.label: A
options.text: Active across most life stages with resilient function and little strong family history.

options.label: B
options.text: Mixed activity and moderate family risk.

Genetic and/or epigenetic predisposition to obesity

options.label: C
options.text: Long low-activity periods, entrenched habits and several affected relatives.
